ateret-zekenim/1:_: They begin to count the omer, etc. Some say not to say "ba'omer" but only "today one day," etc. (Imrei Noam).
ateret-zekenim/9:_: Shabbat night and Yom Tov, etc. If still an hour and a half until night — forbidden to count. One who does not wish to change custom practiced years to count always after Kaddish — congregation forces synagogue to pray after 23 hours until time of berachah in safeik of darkness (responsa Maharshal 13).
biur-halacha/1:א: (1) After the evening prayer - he wrote in the book Mor and Ketzea on the basis of desuprin after the prayer because the early Devodors had the custom to pray the evening prayer before the night and at the end of the Maariv the night began and there were no suprin at the beginning of the night indeed in the law of Ya'akov sek 16 Damdina wrote that one should precede Kash and a prayer that is frequent:
biur-halacha/1:ב: To count the omer — behold Rambam and Chinuch hold it applies from the Torah even now; indeed Tur and Shulchan Aruch and several poskim hold it is not nowadays but a remembrance of the Temple when they offered the omer; and so is the sugya of poskim in this siman; indeed Rambam is not alone in his view, for R' Yeshaya likewise — see Shulchan Aruch Mechaber beginning siman 234; and R' Binyamin there end of siman — see there; and Ravyah brought in Or Zaru'a siman 329 — it is implied Or Zaru'a also concedes to his law — see there; and from words of Rav Yehudai and Rav Amram and Ritz Giat who agreed to their words brought in Ittur that if he did not count from evening he lost — we are strict on temimot — it appears from the Torah and not merely remembrance; Ittur rejected their words because counting the omer for us is not d'oraisa since now there is no offering nor sacrifice and no precision in temimot — it appears for them it is d'oraisa [one may say somewhat they hold although only remembrance of Temple the rabbis made it like d'oraisa specifically temimot]; therefore great support for our custom that we are careful not to count until stars emerge, since per many authorities it is d'oraisa; afterward I found similar in Avodat Yom Tov except he did not mention all these great ones we wrote
biur-halacha/1:ג: And mitzvah on each one etc. — see Mishna Berurah what I wrote — dispute of Acharonim whether we say in this "one who hears is as one who speaks" — dispute of Levush and Chayei Adam with Peri Chadash; Levush and Chayei Adam like lulav we expound "and you shall take for yourselves" for each one — so too here each must count himself; Peri Chadash is lenient; and so inclines Birkei Yosef; in my opinion this is dispute among Rishonim: Rashi explained there Menachot 65b on what the Gemara says for each one — each is obligated to count; and in Chiddushei Rashba his words imply if Torah's intent is only the congregation and not each individual — it should say "and you shall count" alone and be silent; and since it says "to you" it implies to say to each one — see there; behold the mitzvah applies to each individual separately; against this early Ritz Giat implies one can fulfill another — there in laws of counting: "and we received from our teachers support for counting the omer standing from 'when the sickle begins in the standing grain' — you need not learn standing grain except standing; and on Motzei Shabbat they say after evening prayer and yihi noam and kedusha of the order while sitting — early ones practiced the prayer leader bless standing and all the congregation answer amen with intent not to trouble the congregation to return and stand" — end; likewise Orchot Chayim in name of R' Hai Gaon — see there; it implies they fulfill through his counting if their intent is they fulfill only through blessing alone — if so they must stand for counting itself which must be standing as above [in my opinion one should examine even per Rashi above where one is not expert to count himself — perhaps another can fulfill him and it is no worse than Birkat HaMazon where one cannot fulfill another per all unless he ate himself because it is written "and you shall eat and be satisfied" — whoever ate blesses; nevertheless we rule one who counts blesses and an ignoramus fulfills; perhaps so here — requires study]; behold we clarified this is dispute of authorities; therefore l'chatchila certainly each must count himself; b'dieved if he heard from another and intended to fulfill he returns and counts without blessing; so too Peri Megadim
biur-halacha/1:ד: He counts and continues — see Acharonim who disputed if he counted in acronyms such as he said today two days etc. whether he fulfilled; Chayei Adam wrote since for most poskim counting nowadays is only d'rabbanan one should not be stringent from uncertainty and return to count without blessing. Know in any case if he blessed in his heart certainly he did not fulfill at all — thought is not like speech; so Peri Chadash explicitly in seif 7; see above siman 62 seif 4 in Mishna Berurah and Biur Halacha there — examine
biur-halacha/2:_: And so is proper to do — see Mishna Berurah if he counted in twilight he fulfilled — so Magen Avraham and other Acharonim; this matter is mentioned in Tosafot Menachot 66 s.v. zachar when is it called twilight — see siman 261 that Shulchan Aruch holds there twilight is three-quarters mil before stars and is about a quarter hour approximately; before that is certainly day — see Biur Halacha s.v. ve-shiur end of Shulchan Aruch HaRav there that even for those who hold twilight begins immediately after sunset — for Shabbat we are stringent like R' Yehuda; but to be lenient even in rabbinic matters requires study whether we can be lenient and say two leniencies: one that it is twilight like R' Yehuda and also rabbinic uncertainty to leniency since for R' Yosi it is certainly day all the time from sunset until near stars — as we say in Gemara Shabbat 34 when twilight of R' Yehuda completes twilight of R' Yosi begins — requires study
biur-halacha/3:א: While still day — see Mishna Berurah and it is implied from them that from plag ha-Minchah all agree he cannot count; know many Acharonim [Levush, Avodat Yom Tov, Chayei Adam, Maamar Mordechai, Nahar Shalom] explain "while still day" — from plag Minchah and above; and what he said he counts with them — because although by essential law since it is not yet night it is not time of counting as in previous seif — nevertheless places practiced leniency because they were accustomed to pray Maariv before dark and feared if they do not count then in congregation and each goes home he will forget from preoccupation and not count and the essence of counting Torah will be nullified; therefore in pressing circumstance one who says counting nowadays is only remembrance of Temple for most poskim one should not be more stringent than Shema and prayer; since they consider this start of night and read Shema and pray Maariv — likewise we should consider night for counting; and he says even a scholar if his heart troubles him lest he be preoccupied and forget to count privately — he may count with congregation but not bless then in any case by essential law it is not time of counting then — only we do not object to custom of those places and so they not be entirely nullified from this mitzvah; and when time arrives at night he blesses and counts — and it is not blessing in vain for first counting is nothing by essential law as above
biur-halacha/3:ב: (ב) And even an artist answered, and so on, Dr. Dee., the High Priest, blessed all the people in his blessing, and the sewing was given to each one for himself and the S.D.D The artist, along with the bee, is certainly intended to be blessed with the fat sphere, and in any case it is proven to go out in the sesphere by the M.M. D.L.D., said they were the most honest ן . . . . . .
biur-halacha/3:ג: And he blesses and counts at night — see Mishna Berurah Peri Megadim wrote on erev Shabbat in congregation those who delay is better than those who precede and say already night and a moment before say great day to accept Shabbat — I call: heavens darkness to light and that light in brief moment to darkness — therefore proper to prevent this etc. — see there
biur-halacha/4:א: If he says to him today such-and-such etc. — see Taz who brought proofs this is as intending not to fulfill; behold his proofs were rejected by Acharonim [see Avodat Yom Tov, Maamar Mordechai, Nahar Shalom]; nevertheless in essence of law one should examine well — Gra holds this seif is only per those who say mitzvot do not require intent; so Peri Chadash; for us who rule mitzvot require intent he must return and bless [and he does not hold like Radbaz to distinguish d'oraisa and d'rabbanan nor Chayei Adam's resolutions in s.k. 16 nor Magen Avraham s.k. 8]; further in my opinion if this was twilight and this respondent is always accustomed to bless specifically at stars emerging — it is reasonable in this manner he explicitly intends not to fulfill and he may return afterward and count with blessing; for practical law requires study
biur-halacha/4:ב: (ב) It is not possible to come back and welcome – but without a blessing, it must be returned and such a gift is proven from Tel Aviv and has been created as the company A. A. B. A.M. needs a gift and what is in between the Suns of Dr. D. D. A.D., who is told as a way of counting, he must return later and serve without a blessing and as a “here” here. And so before, between the Suns, there was simply another part of the guiding faction, and the responder has already prayed that the respondent should not be worsen in such a way, and can return later And to welcome when the time of the count comes, this opinion of another rejected faction is the essence of the law and I will make it worse:
biur-halacha/6:_: Or the reverse that they are four and he opened etc. and erred and concluded with five etc. — see Mishna Berurah Acharonim wondered on this; Taz resolved Mechaber does not mean he concluded on counting itself but on blessing — meaning at start of blessing when he said "Blessed are You, our Heaven, King of the world" he thought he would count afterward four and only at conclusion of blessing it seemed to him the day is fifth of the omer and he concluded the blessing intending to count five of the omer — he does not return and bless, for we follow opening; and in first case Mechaber depicted similarly — there reason we follow conclusion and because it is rabbinic matter we follow both to leniency and he does not return and bless — Acharonim codified this law (see Darkhei Halacha and Avodat Yom Tov); but Taz derived new law: where opening and conclusion were with intent to count day 5 and after finishing blessing he learned the day is day 4 — he returns and blesses; in this law several Acharonim did not agree — see Mishna Berurah and Sha'arei Teshuvah
biur-halacha/7:_: Forget, and so on, and “If he has a doubt on the day if he is a book at night or not so, he must count [the evidence]:
biur-halacha/8:א: (א) He counts on other days — meaning he holds days do not impede each other; though written "temimot tehiyena," R. Yitzchak Gi'at wrote in the name of R. Hai Gaon: he fulfills temimot in weeks — in each complete week when saying the week's count he fulfills "seven weeks temimot tehiyena"; he also answered there: if one day was lost, count on the second night two countings — e.g. if he forgot the first count, on the second count say "yesterday was one in the omer, and today is two in the omer" — since he also counted yesterday's, he is not excluded from temimot tehiyena — see there, and so in Shulchan Aruch with variation in Shibbolei Leket in the name of responsa of Geonim — see there siman 234; however other poskim did not mention this view and wrote "temimot tehiyena" refers to each day he began counting from evening, as we expound in Menachot 66 and Megillah 20, not that all days impede each other [see Tosafot Menachot and Megillah and Shulchan Aruch in the name of R. Yeshaya and Or Zaru'a siman 329]; in Eshel Avraham I found he wrote it is good to be concerned for R. Hai Gaon's second answer and count yesterday's count together. And without berachah — as above. Other Acharonim did not mention this.
biur-halacha/8:ב: Without blessing — Nahar Shalom wrote one whose deceased lies before him on one of the omer days counts by day after burial without blessing; and it is not similar to prayer one does not pray as makeup as in Yoreh De'ah siman 341 since essentially he was exempt; here per those who count it even by day it is not makeup for night but his obligation extends until end of the festival as implied Rambam chapter 7 Laws of Festivals; and similar to havdalah one makes havdalah on day 1 after burial of deceased whose essential time is until day 4; therefore one who counts by day can count remaining days with blessing; however if burial extended all day such that he had no leisure to count after burial — he should not count further days with blessing — what difference if he forgot to count or deceased prevented counting — either way not temimot — see there; what he decided for one obligated to count by day is not from makeup reason — see Or Zaru'a siman 329 what is written in name of Abba ha-Ezri; in essence of law what is ruled an onen is exempt — Rav Nuv'ei Mahadura Kama 8 Orach Chayim 27 is uncertain per Maharshal responsum 70 that not from all matters is onen exempt; he gathers some reasons one may say also from counting not exempt; primarily because he is not preoccupied and not nullified for this moment from engaging with deceased; he combines also view of some poskim onen exempt but permitted to fulfill; per all this his view he counts while deceased before him without blessing and again can count all days with blessing since without this some poskim do not require temimot at all — see there; Rav Akiva Eiger copied in his glosses
biur-halacha/8:ג: He counts on remaining days with blessing — see Mishna Berurah what is written regarding if he erred in days etc. — Taz's words; although he only cited erred in days and not weeks — it is obvious likewise and all the more erred in weeks and not days since days impede more than weeks for all — as in Mishna Berurah s.k. 7; so Peri Megadim; nevertheless per reasoning it appeared Taz deals only with remaining weekdays that do not impede that he also mention days as Acharonim agreed [see Chayei Adam s.k. 8]; therefore one may say likewise if he erred in it — no worse than not mentioning at all; unlike day completing weeks where by law he must mention days and it impedes as s.k. 7; if so obvious likewise if he erred in counting days his counting is nothing and is as if entirely skipped and counts remaining days without blessing; possible Taz's view even on days completing weeks one may be lenient for upcoming countings since for many poskim days do not impede each other — if so at least one may be lenient when he mentioned one of the numbers — days or weeks; see Avodat Yom Tov who also questioned Taz's essential law — requires study for practical law; Peri Megadim also spoke on this and there are printing errors in his words and I could not understand his view
biur-halacha/10:_: Even in our time — see Mishna Berurah what is written we cannot protest those who are lenient — so many Acharonim; they sided finding reason for world custom as Mishna Berurah wrote; nevertheless since it is known many who are careful regarding any prohibition in other prohibitions are also lenient here — I saw the reason is they think whoever wants to be careful must be careful in all stringencies of guards and wages and also in purging vessels — difficult to be careful in these countries; therefore each relies on world custom to be entirely lenient; but in my opinion it is not proper because difficulty in all stringencies should not make entirely lenient; behold in flour it is easy to be careful as today found everywhere wheat flour sown in Cheshvan (and I heard from acquaintances good wheat flour sown in Poland are all sown in Cheshvan and those from Volhynia majority are old from those sown in Cheshvan); also from presumption possibly majority are old; and in beer several Acharonim side to leniency — see Penei Yehoshua and Mishkenot Yaakov and other Acharonim; also beer is not certainly new for even in winter months beer is sometimes made from old barley malt (and although many great Acharonim are stringent also on beer as explained Yoreh De'ah and Acharonim there — lenient have whom to rely on); in doubt we have Or Zaru'a who wrote one may rely in pressing circumstance on those who hold new grain d'rabbanan and it is rabbinic doubt; likewise in purging vessels and lees there are sides to leniency; but in the groats themselves of barley and oats in our country they are certainly new in winter; although we cannot protest world custom to be lenient as Acharonim wrote — proper and correct to be stringent for oneself at least in this; behold for great Rishonim it is d'oraisa — Rif, Rosh, Rambam, Semag, Ittur, Mordechai, in name of Ravyah, Hagahot Maimoniyot, Ritva; and even Or Zaru'a who sides d'rabbanan in chutz la-aretz did not rely to be lenient except in doubt — then one may rely in pressing circumstance on those who hold d'rabbanan and it is double doubt; but not certainly new; Terumat HaDeshen also wrote thus; Peskei Tosafot Menachot wrote of gentiles' grain it is d'rabbanan — if so at least d'rabbanan; nevertheless forbidden; we have no lenient ones except R' Baruch Baal HaTosafot who wrote to be lenient in distant places abroad; Ma'aleh Tzedek in name of R' Avigdor Cohen in name of Rivash wrote to be lenient entirely on gentiles' grain as brought in Bach — they are individual against all these authorities; also several lenient Acharonim did not wish to be lenient except in doubt not certainly; Shulchan Aruch here and Yoreh De'ah sealed like poskim it is d'oraisa in all respects; many Acharonim also grasped thus for essence; therefore certainly proper and correct to be concerned for all this and separate at least from certainly new as above; whoever wishes to give heart to this can obtain in winter from these species from old produce
chatam-sofer/1:_: The author of R. R. N.A. has written a page by writing a taste of why there are no writers because of Spike Dioma in his book.
chatam-sofer/2:_: (there in Magen Avraham s.k. 90) that the last day is always deferred — marginal note: and regarding temimot see Mishnah 4 chapter 4 of Sanhedrin and see in HaRa'avad and Tosefot Yom Tov there
chatam-sofer/3:_: (there s.k. 1) One must count the day; therefore one does not bless — as it should read
chatam-sofer/4:_: (there in Magen Avraham s.k. 2) He counts by himself — marginal note: and it is not similar to taking the lulav, for a mitzvah performed by one's body such as donning tefillin and taking the lulav — one cannot fulfill for another; unlike a mitzvah through speech, one who hears is as one who speaks — see Kapos Temarim Sukkah daf 41b; and that which we say "and you shall count" — the counting shall be for each one — is to exclude counting the Jubilee, which is only for the great court in Jerusalem, as Tosafot wrote Menachot daf 65b s.v. ve-sefaratem etc., see there; and see Chiddushei Sofer Orach Chayim siman 210
chatam-sofer/5:_: (there in Taz s.k. 10) with havdalah and counted before kiddush — marginal note: Taz's reasoning is not so strong, for in kiddush he does not interrupt the sanctity of seven and it is not comparable to havdalah that separates between the sanctity of Shabbat and the sanctity of Yom Tov. And examine. It appears to me by reasoning that one should precede counting the omer, per what Magen Avraham s.k. 1 wrote that the counting is not a contradiction; and further since we are expert in fixing the month, counting is primary — therefore one blesses; and for this reason there is indeed a contradiction, only that perforce one must bless; and one may say that in any case one should precede counting, which is by law, and not precede kiddush, for he has already taken hold of Yom Tov — and then counting is said in contradiction; unlike if he precedes counting, then kiddush, which is custom, is said in contradiction and we are not so concerned, as above — examine. But Chayei Adam already wrote the custom is to sanctify first; see in Peri Megadim
chatam-sofer/6:_: In two orders as well — marginal note: see Tosafot Avodah Zarah beginning of chapter Ein Ma'amidin, Rosh beginning of chapter Kol HaBasar
chatam-sofer/7:_: (there s.k. 17) and Mishna Berurah holds — marginal note: for R' Baruch, so it should read
chokhmat-shlomo/8:_: Seif 8: But if he is uncertain whether he skipped one day and did not count, he counts on the remaining days with a blessing. Marginal note: see the source of this law in Terumat HaDeshen and its reason and rationale there; and see in Chiddushei Halachot Berachot siman 295, and it is in my works on Orach Chayim from the year 5637 in responsum to the community of Michanovka near Barditchev on whether one blesses on s'chach — examine well
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [א] [Levush] He does not fulfill, etc. So Agudah in chapter R' Yishmael: "you shall count for yourselves" — for each one, not agent of congregation for all; so Rashba 126: if he intends to fulfill he counts without berachah if he does not interrupt — see siman 8 Talit. In Eliyah Zuta I questioned: "you shall count for yourselves" excludes yovel count entrusted to court as Kelbo and Abudraham wrote; whence that if one intends to fulfill for another and other intends to fulfill, he does not fulfill sefirah, since we hold shome'a ke'oneh for kiddush and mitzvot dependent on speech — unlike lulav "you shall take" — taking for each one, not speech-dependent; siman 658 I wrote perhaps learned gezeirah shavah from "count" to "take" — requires study.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [ב] Standing, etc. If he counted seated he fulfilled (Rambam, Rokeach). There: women and slaves exempt — positive time-bound; Magen Avraham: nevertheless already obligatory; some say Psalm Elohim yichaneinu immediately after count as Maaglei Tzedek wrote.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [ג] To bless, etc. Ran questioned end Sukkah: how bless on counting on second Yom Tov without Yom Tov degradation, as no berachah on sukkah on Shemini Atzeret — answered: there on cup "this festival day" — sukkah berachah would contradict; here opposite — we are expert in month fixing, by law no sitting in sukkah on Shemini Atzeret — no berachah; here by law must count today — we bless. Do not question: before havdalah forbidden to degrade — if so on Shemini Atzeret with kiddush too — no degradation.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [ד] Days and weeks, etc. In Eliyah Zuta I brought Rabbeinu Yerucham p. 44: why not two berachot — days and weeks are two mitzvot like tefillin of hand and head; why say "they are one week" — say "today one week"; appears because "seven weeks" is written — week counting written only by omer, day counting not by omer — days are Torah even now, week counting without omer is only Temple remembrance, and for remembrance alone one does not bless as Passover wrapping; therefore "they are one week" — not real counting; if truly counting as in omer times berachah would return for weeks — end quote; Beit Yosef and Acharonim distinguished this month; fit to rule if he forgot days though counted weeks he must return and bless; specifically end of each week; mid-week some hold no need even l'chatchila except "today one week and one day" — though we do not hold so, do not return and bless — below sk 14.
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: [ה] [Levush] Today second, etc. He said "today two days" or twelve or thirteen — return to count without berachah (Knesset HaGedolah).
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [ו] Fourteen, etc. Smaller number first; where they count larger first — per local custom (Acharonim). Rest of Knesset HaGedolah lengthy; in our lands even secular tongue — smaller first. Permitted any language understood; if not Holy Tongue — do not count in Holy Tongue (Magen Avraham). Shibulei Leket: until ten "days," from eleven "day" — elegance in Holy Tongue (Amek Berachah). Some say Psalm after count. Maharil: at 49 say they are seven weeks.
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [ז] [Levush] He should not say "that today," etc. In Eliyah Zuta I brought many formulas with "today" — those who practice so should not be protested; those saying ba'omer or la'omer both have great authority — see responsa Beit Yaakov 23.
eliyah-rabbah/8:_: [ח] [Levush] We do not bless time, etc. Abudraham: world in distress from Passover until Shavuot over grain and trees — therefore commanded to count these days to remember world's distress and return with whole heart to plead mercy on grain. Another reason: each Israelite busy in harvest days — commanded to count to know when Shavuot; also allusion to seventh millennium all Shabbat; therefore seventh day of Passover is Atzeret, Shavuot after seven weeks, Shemini Atzeret alludes to world to come and great yovel — Rabbeinu Yerucham; beside the way I found ancients had seven planetary deities and Balaam offered seven altars — each has seven dominions totaling forty-nine — Torah given in fifty and commanded not to serve them — the Holy One tore seven heavens and opened seven lands to show no deity besides Him.
eliyah-rabbah/9:_: [ט] [Levush] To the day they left, etc. If you say count from day one — it appears day one was entirely for remembering the great miracle of Exodus, proof of creation and Divine providence — we should not mix other matters in our joy. Do not say "today such-and-such" on second Passover night lest the count be unfit to say "second day"; therefore fixed ba'omer as remembrance we believe the Omnipresent renews grain yearly (Sefer HaChinuch).
eliyah-rabbah/10:_: [י] They return to count, etc. With berachah; if from plag haMinchah onward return and count without berachah — see there, requires study; appears specifically after ma'ariv; before ma'ariv count with berachah; if counted twilight fulfilled — counting rabbinic, safeik rabbinic lenient; however per above Rabbeinu Yerucham days counting d'oraisa — fit to return count without berachah; Ran end Pesachim cites many who hold d'oraisa — therefore our custom not to count even publicly until stars.
eshel-avraham/1:_: He counts and continues. If he said "today forty minus one of the omer" he fulfilled — see Turei Zahav end of siman 10
eshel-avraham/8:_: Blessing. And if he wrote on that day the days of counting that he wrote "today such-and-such days and weeks of the omer" he does not fulfill — for it is not like speech — see Turei Zahav what is written siman 20; and if he was an onen at night he counts after burial without blessing, and the night after — it is obvious he blesses — see Devar Moshe siman 33 and Yoreh De'ah siman 228 and Yad Efraim siman 3731
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: א) [Seif 1] Second night, etc. They say ma'arivim of second night even if first day Shabbat — other festivals: first on Shabbat — second night ma'arivim of first day, second postponed; second day Passover always ma'arivim of that day for omer priority. Levush. Magen Avraham head of siman. Kaf HaChayyim 1. Chok Yosef 1. So too Simchat Torah Motzei Shabbat — ma'arivim of Shemini Atzeret though rain mentioned. Why not ma'arivim on Shabbat — not expert in rain causing tilt. Or Samech 1 — Ashkenazim and Sephardim differ. א"א head of siman — so for both customs.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: ב) There. They begin counting omer. Kesef Mishnah ch. 6 Sukkah: how bless on second Yom Tov without degradation — on Shemini Atzeret no sukkah berachah — answered: there on cup "this festival day" contradicts sukkah berachah; not here. Or not expert in month fixing — no sukkah on Shemini Atzeret — no berachah; here must count by law — bless. Bach. Magen Avraham sk 1. Ran end Sukkah. Kaf HaChayyim 2 — more answers see there.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: ג) There. They begin to count, etc. Reason no "shehecheyanu" on omer count — only remembrance, remembrance of Temple; also no joy found in berachat zman except matters with pleasure — lulav for joy, shofar remembrance, megillah compassion and redemption, pidyon haben father's joy child survived thirty days. Ran end Pesachim in Sefer HaMe'or — see there; Rashba 126. Levush: counting for Yom Tov need, rely on festival time — see other reasons in Acharonim — not lengthy.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: ד) There. They begin to count, etc. "Whoever does not count is not of the seven complete weeks for purity" — Zohar Emor 97b — see there; besides bittul mitzvah for those who hold d'oraisa as below.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: ה) There. They begin to count, etc. Most poskim: sefirat haomer today only rabbinic — remembrance of Temple when they offered omer on 16 Nisan and counted from bringing omer — as Amemar Menachot R' Yishmael: remembrance of Temple alone, therefore count days not weeks; other amoraim there count days and weeks — not arguing on Amemar fundamentally but mitzvah in general Israel counts days and weeks — Rishonim. However Rambam ch. 7 Temidim, Chinuch: mitzvah of sefirat haomer even today d'oraisa; Rabbis of Rav Ashi's academy count days and weeks — argue on Amemar, not mere remembrance but d'oraisa — rule like them, infer from gemara language "Amemar said count days not weeks — it is remembrance of Temple" — not fixed halachah. Kaf HaChayyim 1. R. Zera 2: primary like those who say today only rabbinic. Chayei Adam klal 131 1.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: ו) There. They begin to count, etc. I have seen meticulous ones on second Yom Tov night do the seder, and after entire seder bless on omer count — reasonable. However by law forbidden to eat until counting, and throughout seder likely to forget. Kaf HaChayyim 5. However Sefer Nehora Hashaleish p. 25b in Nefesh Hashaleish: diaspora must bless omer berachah second Yom Tov night immediately after ma'ariv, for sefirah is d'oraisa mitzvah and seder is rabbinic — each has its aspect — do not delay after seder lest give foothold to externals — see chaverim 2.
kaf-hachayyim/7:א: (א) ז) There. Before counting good to say parashat haomer in Emor and Vayedaber... until "new meal offering to the Omnipresent," then Yoma R' Yishmael omer, etc. — see above 429:6, below 494:5. Then say formula in Rashash siddur — chasidim of Beit El follow Ari.
kaf-hachayyim/7:ב: (ב) ז) For unification... I come to fulfill positive mitzvah of sefirat haomer days and weeks (night 49 skip until "repair its root") [as written count for yourselves from morrow of rest day... seven complete weeks until morrow of seventh week count fifty days] to repair root above. May it be will before You, Master of the universe... that now be time of mercy to raise this omer count as if attaining all sealed secrets therein with intentions of Your beloved knowing holy names in this count... strengthen in this count's segulah and two great luminaries with small, fill chambers with understanding, increase knowledge for the warriors of Heaven. Also give good and our land yield.
kaf-hachayyim/7:ג: (ג) ז) And may it be will... repair what we damaged in supernal attributes... one unity (night 49 skip) [seven complete weeks] on one stone seven eyes (Shabbat and Yom Tov night skip "and forgive") forgive all sins from youth until today. As You purified Israel at Exodus from Egyptian impurity by omer count power, purify our souls from all impurity and illness, sanctify with supernal holiness. As omer stood for Israel shield in Gideon's days, Chizkiyahu, Yechezkel, Mordechai and Esther to subdue enemies — waving fought them — so stand for us against soul enemies and seekers of evil. Wondrous mercies, save the oppressed today. Arouse might for salvation...
kaf-hachayyim/8:_: ח) After berachah say "HaRachaman may He return Temple service to its place speedily in our days." Tosafot Megillah 20b s.v. kol. Intend berachah draws surrounding light; "HaRachaman" action aspect as in Temple draws inner light. Then Ana bechoach... each night standing; when saying psalm intend each night letter alef of Elohim night one, yechaneinu night two, etc. until 49; likewise letter of "yismachu veyranenu"; Ana bekoach first night alef, second beit, etc. six days; night seven acronym of whole verse abg ytz... second week kuf resh... until seven weeks — see Shaar HaKavanot drush 11, Pokeach 22:3,5. See below 106, above 1:22, below 494:8.
kaf-hachayyim/9:_: ט) There. They begin to count, etc. Women exempt — positive time-bound. Rambam ch. 7. Zohar Tzav 183a. Shaar HaKavanot 85b. Magen Avraham sk 1. Women already obligatory. Kaf HaChayyim 3. R. Avraham 2. Chok Yosef 3. R. Zera 2. However Maharshal Sha'ar Aryeh manuscript, Maharil manuscript protest women counting; Bach 22: women if practice lulav should practice sefirah per custom — end quote. R. Zera: no prohibition if they bless though exempt. Shelah Shelomo: at least do not bless, for surely err day one and do not know word meanings. Bach. Mishna Berurah 3. Ashkenaz women bless on time-bound mitzvot as 489:6 — Sephardi women without berachah if they wish to fulfill — hear from men, intend, then count.
kaf-hachayyim/10:_: י) There. They begin to count, etc. Though yovel also "count for yourself" and zavah "she shall count" — Rabbis learned this "you shall count" by omer is actual count, unlike other countings — Ran end Pesachim. Taz sk 1. See Tosafot Menachot 65b s.v. vesaperatem; below 108.
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 1) Kesef Mishnah challenged — see: Ran wrote at the end of Pesachim and at the end of Sukkah
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif 1: One begins to count. If counting in writing — is it counting? See Teshuvot Magen Shmuel siman 20. If he counted by way of twenty minus one he fulfilled — responsum Pri HaEretz to Maharam Mizrachi siman 10. That which one does not bless shehecheyanu on counting the omer — see responsum Radbaz siman 54
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 2: And if he wishes, one who hears the blessing. It is good that one bless and fulfill others to fulfill "in the multitude of the people is the glory of the king" — see above siman 288 seif 18. See responsum Mahari Weil siman 280
rabbi-akiva-eiger/7:_: Seif 7: If he forgot and did not bless all night — if a deceased fell to him at night and the burial ground is distant such that he is an onen all night and the next day he counts the entire day without blessing, and on the days after he counts with blessing — responsum Noda B'Yehuda siman 27
rabbi-akiva-eiger/9:_: Seif 9: one should count before blessing. Source in Terumat HaDeshen; in my opinion one should discuss for halacha that Terumat HaDeshen may hold like poskim that havdalah is rabbinic, but per Rama's rulings above siman 471 seif 5 he interrupts a meal for havdalah — therefore he holds havdalah is d'oraisa, as Magen Avraham siman 239 wrote (and Rama siman 296 that two should not make havdalah for themselves is l'chatchila to be concerned for stringency of those who hold havdalah rabbinic, and women are exempt, but from essence of law men make havdalah for themselves, havdalah d'oraisa of "remember" at entry and exit, and women are obligated, for all included in guarding are included). One may say havdalah comes first; and though in all places counting comes first because of yoma adif over the view of precedence of d'oraisa, and proof from Kiddushin Nazir — even though Kiddush of Yom Tov is rabbinic as Magen Avraham siman 471, nevertheless one may say in Musaf of Yom Tov regarding counting there is yu'lei yoma in Kiddush and yoma adif in havdalah stands in law to precede d'oraisa; and truly what is written in Musaf of weekday also has proof to precede counting to havdalah from Kiddushin Nazir — there are two elevations: one yu'lei yoma of Kiddush and one yoma adif of havdalah — therefore they precede rabbinic Kiddush before d'oraisa havdalah; and though Rama did not emend thus and Mechaber appears to hold havdalah d'oraisa from his words siman 296 that women are obligated in havdalah — since Rama ruled here seif 4 the Posek from eating to counting and is concerned for those who hold counting today d'oraisa, therefore he holds here like Terumat HaDeshen they count first; but per Magen Avraham here sk 26 if he erred and counted in Maariv he fulfilled since we are not concerned for poskim who say he did not fulfill, and it is proper to count from darkening without berachah since not great effort, for he holds essence of counting today is rabbinic — then great proof is needed to precede rabbinic counting before d'oraisa havdalah, since against yoma adif there is also yu'lei yoma — uncertain.
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: On — Ba'er Heitev; and see in She'elat Ya'avetz siman 139 who disagrees that even if he does not understand in the holy tongue he fulfilled — see there
shaarei-teshuvah/6:_: And the weeks. Avi Ezra HaTov: if he counted in initials like yud-alef, lamed-gimmel ba'omer — view of Gi'at siman 526 he fulfilled; Peri Chadash and some Acharonim, and in She'elat Yaavetz siman 239 agreed he did not fulfill; in Birkei Yosef he wrote his view leans this way and good to return and count without berachah; if he counted in initials with full letters like yud-alef etc., She'elat Yaavetz wrote he returns and counts without berachah — see there; see Birkei Yosef if he wrote a letter to his friend and wrote yom-tet-bet for counting — obvious he must return and count orally with berachah; see there laws of writing whether it is like speech he brought from siman 46 regarding Birkat HaTorah and Shav Yaakov part 10 siman 49 and Knesset HaGedolah siman 210 — see there; in my opinion clear that even if he wrote "seventeen days that are" etc. he did not fulfill at all unless he intended to fulfill through this writing — slight room to examine, and it appears here too he should return and count with berachah, and it is not like other places where even if we say writing is like speech, it is where speech itself is only to reveal thought of the heart, unlike here; and as it does not help if one writes Shema and prayer, and Megillah clearly requires oral reading as we say "if he was writing" etc.; see below siman 498; see Eshel Avraham who showed place for responsum on what was written on this matter; see Shirurei Berachah who wrote one who counted in initials tet-vav-bet that afterward he will be shaliach tzibbur and bless to fulfill others — see there; in our country we did not practice fulfilling through shaliach tzibbur berachah at all, only each blesses and counts for himself — therefore he should not be shaliach tzibbur and bless since he is only for himself and must count without berachah.
shaarei-teshuvah/8:_: In the omer. Ba'er Heitev; and see in responsum Beit Yaakov that his father-in-law the gaon would say "to the omer" and he upheld the nusach "to the omer" and brought proof from Chayei Adam siman 253 — see there; but in truth there is no proof from there to here; and we find in the language of Scripture "in the second year of their going out" and similar; it is better "to the omer" with the lamed, and so is practiced in our country per the Ari; and see in Even HaEzer siman 126 regarding writing a get for the month — see there
shaarei-teshuvah/10:_: 49. Ba'er Heitev; and see in Chayei Adam who wrote in the name of Maharil that when he reaches day 49 he says they are seven weeks and the next day is erev Shavuot — this is astonishing, for it implies he says so at the time of counting, and this is not so; this wording "and the next day" etc. is the language of Lekutei Maharil who wrote this as the manner of customs that day 49 is erev Shavuot, but not that one says so at the time of counting; and in responsum Shevut Yaakov part 3 they challenged him and he strained to prove from what is written "and the next day" etc., and it is not so; and likewise the practice of the people is that they do not say this at all
yad-ephraim/1:_: (Taz sk 7) and on this Rosh there is uncertain, for Rosh there relies on what Rif wrote and those who bless in Birkat HaMazon — namely when he first does so in his house — see above siman 484; and one may say it also refers if he first does so in another's house, for Rif wrote afterward; nevertheless it is clear there that he did not taste with them — how can one say he fulfilled Birkat HaMazon; also what he brought proof from lulav for a minor — uncertain, for there with lulav in the minor's hand one cannot say he fulfilled with it; I found in Eliyah Rabbah he challenged the proof from lulav for a minor — see there.
